name: Dihydroetorphine
summary: Dihydroetorphine was developed by K. W. Bentley at McFarlan-Smith in the 1960s and is a potent opioid analgesic used mainly in China. It is a derivative of the better-known opioid etorphine, a very potent veterinary painkiller and anesthetic medication used primarily for the sedation of large animals such as elephants, giraffes, and rhinos.

pharmacology.text: Regulation elsewhere may vary but would likely be similar to that for other strong opioid agonists.
